candidates.name: Joint purchase of prospective rare disease evidence
candidates.beneficiary_value: Small patient foundations and competing therapy developers obtain otherwise underfunded, interoperable longitudinal evidence without duplicating scarce patients' reporting burden.
candidates.missing_outcome: Several sponsors commit funding for one prospectively specified cohort and common measurements, governed by patients, with transparent access and cost allocation.
candidates.prior_art_and_specific_gap: RDCA-DAP already standardizes shared data and governs access; recreating a repository has little novelty. Its FAQ distinguishes integration of existing data from collecting new prospective data and notes sustainability and consent obstacles. The proposed gap is joint financing of missing observations before they exist. [S5,S6]
candidates.what_changed: FDA's March 2026 workshop explicitly examined fragmented rare disease data and legal/logistical sharing barriers. Agents could compare protocols and identify the smallest shared measurement set, but clinical validity still requires experts. [S7]
candidates.discovered_connection: An advance purchase agreement can fund an evidence public good: multiple prospective beneficiaries finance common observations, while an existing trusted platform receives appropriately consented data.
candidates.minimal_construction_falsifier: Using public protocols, choose one disease and map three sponsors' endpoint and eligibility requirements. Produce a prospective common dataset specification, consent requirements and cost allocation. Reject if incompatible populations or measurement schedules remove meaningful reuse. Synthetic bias tests cannot demonstrate that an external control is clinically valid.
candidates.commercial_mechanism: Sponsors fund cohort operations and pay governance/service fees; patient organizations retain representation. No patient-data sale is required. Competitive incentives, consent, clinical costs and regulator acceptance can defeat the model.
candidates.successor_inheritance: Preserve endpoint mappings, consent restrictions, protocol versions, missingness assumptions and documented reasons cohorts cannot be combined.
candidates.uncertainty: Highest potential human value but weakest immediate validation. Existing consortia and registry providers may already supply the financing arrangement.

candidates.name: A pooled option to restart supply of an unattractive generic medicine
candidates.status: Do not advance without a narrower uncovered gap
candidates.beneficiary_value: Patients and small providers need predictable access when ordinary unit sales do not support redundant supply.
candidates.binding_restriction_stranded_resource: Readiness and validation cost money even when demand is uncertain; individually small purchasers cannot cover them. Potentially stranded licensed capacity must be demonstrated, not presumed.
candidates.specific_prior_art_limitation: The initial demand-assurance proposal is substantially anticipated by Civica's long-term commitments and stockpiles (S4), including support for rural hospitals. Only a validated restart option outside existing coverage might remain; no evidence establishes that gap.
candidates.enabling_change: Agents might reduce multi-party specification and commitment-assembly costs, but cannot supply licensed production, validated readiness or regulatory approval.
candidates.connection_discovered: Separate payment for continued production readiness from payment per delivered unit, with allocation rights agreed before a shortage.
candidates.construction_falsifier: Select one publicly documented supply failure, establish an uncovered purchaser group and a legally usable backup producer, then price readiness against inventory and Civica membership. Reject absent available validated capacity or if existing alternatives dominate. This test was not run.
candidates.commercial_mechanism: Purchasers pay a readiness retainer only below expected disruption and inventory costs; producer needs retained fees to cover validation, opportunity cost and availability obligations. Neither willingness to pay nor positive surplus was observed.
candidates.successor_inheritance: A strong negative novelty result, supplier-readiness requirements and a break-even template; avoid repeatedly rediscovering generic procurement pooling.

candidates.name: Conditional transformer reserve rights for smaller utilities
candidates.beneficiary_value: Small municipal and cooperative utilities obtain credible access to replacement large power transformers without each financing a complete independent reserve. Residents benefit from faster restoration. This concerns reserve access, not manufacturing inspection.
candidates.missing_outcome: A utility can know before an emergency exactly which replacement it may call, under which simultaneous emergencies, with transport and owner-retention conditions already agreed.
candidates.prior_art_and_specific_gap: GAO documents STEP, SpareConnect, RESTORE and Grid Assurance; pooling is established. SpareConnect leaves transaction terms bilateral, STEP has specified emergency triggers, and Grid Assurance owns inventory. GAO found limited smaller-utility participation. The narrower unproven gap is affordable, precommitted access to existing heterogeneous spares while preserving each owner's minimum protection. [S1]
candidates.what_changed: GAO's May 2026 update still reports an open participation recommendation, while DOE is developing common-equipment information. Capable agents could maintain detailed evidence and agreement dependencies economically across small participants; that cost advantage remains a hypothesis. [S2]
candidates.discovered_connection: Treat a spare as a bundle of mutually compatible contingent access rights. Combine technical compatibility evidence with cooperative risk allocation: a nameplate match alone cannot establish availability when several owners suffer together.
candidates.minimal_construction_falsifier: Build a local rights ledger with explicit asset identifiers, technical evidence, dispatch deadlines, owner-retention rules and disaster scenarios. Enumerate allocations and emit either an auditable assignment or a concrete conflicting-claims witness. Then populate one class using public specifications; unknown compatibility must reject certification. Kill the opportunity if credible compatibility plus transport eliminates pooling savings, or an incumbent already offers equivalent terms economically to the target segment.
candidates.commercial_mechanism: A utility association sponsors the pool; participating utilities pay annual reservation and administration fees, while contributing owners receive reservation revenue. Initial paid work would be engineering-backed feasibility. No willingness to pay, insurability or enforceability has been established.
candidates.successor_inheritance: Versioned compatibility evidence, scenario exclusions, contract dependencies, counterexamples and verified commitments become reusable operational state. Successors can add participants without silently invalidating old promises.
candidates.uncertainty: Moderate evidence of underserved users; low evidence of this precise product gap. Real inventories and binding commitments are unavailable. Older program descriptions require direct rechecking before launch.

candidates.name: Conditional neighborhood commitments for shared thermal networks
candidates.beneficiary_value: Residents, small building owners and municipalities obtain a financeable shared heating/cooling project where isolated retrofits and speculative studies leave collective infrastructure unbuilt.
candidates.missing_outcome: A neighborhood can conditionally commit enough demand, access rights and anchor participation to justify engineering expenditure while capping each participant's tariff and cancellation exposure.
candidates.prior_art_and_specific_gap: NYSERDA already supports stakeholder outreach, technical design, ownership and financing; DOE already funds community coalitions. The proposed gap is a single conditional closing arrangement linking those dependencies, rather than another feasibility report. Sources establish coordination work, not the absence of such contracts. [S3,S4]
candidates.what_changed: DOE reports three installations progressing from eleven planning projects, supplying contemporary precedents. Agent-assisted comparison of building constraints, stakeholder terms and financing conditions may make smaller coalitions economical. No inference that the other eight projects failed is warranted. [S4]
candidates.discovered_connection: Infrastructure financing resembles a threshold public-good problem: nobody should bear full early commitment risk before enough complementary participants join. An assurance contract can make a technically plausible cluster investable.
candidates.minimal_construction_falsifier: Create a 12-building synthetic closing simulation with individual price ceilings, anchor withdrawal, easement failure and cost overruns. Require automatic cancellation/refund whenever any essential condition fails. Reconstruct one public pilot's disclosed economics. Reject if the arrangement cannot survive one plausible anchor exit, or if measured participation costs dominate savings. Real adoption requires later participant testing.
candidates.commercial_mechanism: Municipalities or developers buy coalition formation; a project entity pays a closing fee only on financial close. Avoid relying on unspecified subsidies. Sales cycles, enforceable household terms and development liability may make the model unattractive.
candidates.successor_inheritance: Carry forward stakeholder-condition graphs, bounded economics, withdrawal scenarios and locally reviewed terms; future agents update the coalition when a participant changes.
candidates.uncertainty: Existing district-energy developers may already solve the proposed gap. Physical feasibility and financing remain dominant constraints.

candidates.name: A jointly contingent right to relocate with replacement housing secured
candidates.status: Provisional recommendation; novelty and enforceability unresolved
candidates.beneficiary_value: Hazard-exposed households can leave together without committing their existing home before a suitable replacement and financing are secured. Municipalities can complete coherent projects rather than leave financing-fragmented cohorts.
candidates.binding_restriction_stranded_resource: A household will not commit without a replacement; sellers will not reserve indefinitely; a municipality may have awarded reimbursement funding but insufficient closing cash. The stranded resource is an approved future payment plus mutually compatible housing transactions.
candidates.specific_prior_art_limitation: S1 already covers collective relocation, land swaps and land banking; S2 already employs professional escrow coordination. The narrower hypothesis is a reusable, independently checkable instrument joining revocable household consent, replacement reservations, grant eligibility, bridge funding and named failure-risk bearers. The inspected sources do not demonstrate that complete instrument; this is not proof it is absent.
candidates.enabling_change: Agents can trace heterogeneous public rules into explicit conditions, construct alternative bundles and adversarially check their cash flows. Actual signatures, valuation, legal authority and underwriting remain human/institutional inputs. Lower assembly cost is a hypothesis, not a measured capability claim.
candidates.connection_discovered: Combine contingent assurance contracts with construction-finance draw conditions and synchronized insured real-estate closing. The valuable output is a new jointly conditional commitment, beyond locating properties or accelerating paperwork.
candidates.construction_falsifier: Construct an eight-household term matrix and escrow state machine: every participant retains withdrawal before closing; replacement and original titles must be jointly ready; approved reimbursement, full bridge and explicit risk coverage must exist; otherwise cancel and charge only the designated sponsor. Local fixture enumerated 24,576 synthetic combinations. Next decisive gate: one public-program dossier must support lawful assignments/guarantees and an affordable complete package. Reject if existing providers already offer the same bundle economically, one required obligation cannot be enforced, households prefer independent moves, or risk-adjusted funding costs exceed avoided delay value.
candidates.commercial_mechanism: A municipality or nonprofit sponsor pays a fixed reviewed-assembly fee and a completion fee; financing is separately priced. Households participate only if their own stated replacement and wealth constraints hold. Sellers receive reservation compensation; lenders receive interest plus explicit loss coverage. The sponsor must prefer these costs to ordinary staggered administration. No subsidy, guarantee, buyer or profit is assumed to exist.
candidates.successor_inheritance: Executable fixture, source-linked condition matrix, typed obligations, outside-option ledger, cancellation counterexamples and rejected novelty claims. Later agents can replace synthetic numbers without inheriting an unsupported claim of viability.

candidates.name: Guaranteed fleet service on a non-firm electricity connection
candidates.beneficiary_value: Small delivery or municipal fleets could begin operation before a firm grid upgrade while buying a specified service commitment.
candidates.binding_restriction_stranded_resource: Available grid capacity is intermittent; the fleet needs reliable departures. Spare charging or vehicle capacity elsewhere cannot support an investment until access is contractually reserved.
candidates.specific_prior_art_limitation: S3 already establishes flexible connections and managed charging; a scheduler is not a discovery. The narrower gap is a jointly purchased fallback charging/vehicle option that backs an enforceable transport-service guarantee. The search did not establish whether charging-as-a-service vendors already supply it.
candidates.enabling_change: Agents could assemble tariff conditions, route constraints, fallback rights and conservative feasibility certificates into an underwritable package; existing engineering control remains necessary.
candidates.connection_discovered: Treat non-firm electricity as an input to a firm transport obligation; reserve substitution rights instead of requiring firm electricity at every depot.
candidates.construction_falsifier: Combine a public connection envelope, disclosed duty cycles and independently confirmed fallback capacities. Test worst-case curtailment and correlated feeder failure, including travel time and simultaneous fallback claims. Reject if the guaranteed routes fail, fallback cannot be exclusively reserved, or premiums exceed waiting/retaining existing vehicles. No such real-data replay was completed here.
candidates.commercial_mechanism: Fleet pays availability premium below its quantified delay cost; fallback operators receive reservation fees above displaced business; guarantor requires premium exceeding correlated tail losses, capital and operations. The grid retains unconditional authority to curtail under its agreement.
candidates.successor_inheritance: Executable service-obligation schemas, capacity reservation graph, adversarial scenarios and explicit correlations; no assumed independence or invented insured capacity.
